newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Eurotunnel debt deal, fire news awaited.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Eurotunnel debt deal, fire news awaited.

text.p: Investors in Eurotunnel Plc will be keenly awaiting an update on the debt restructuring deal and the fall-out from last November's tunnel fire next Thursday, when the group is expected to report narrower annual losses.

Pre-tax losses for the year to December 31 1996, are forecast to come in between 650 million and 700 million stg, according to data from Edinburgh Financial Products for Reuters 3000 and Reuters' consensus figures.
The average forecast is for a loss of 662.5 million compared with 924.8 million in losses for the previous year.
Analysts said investors will be hoping for news of the deal on Eurotunnel's nine billion stg of debt.
Earlier this week, the Financial Times reported that the steering committee of leading bankers to Eurotunnel had agreed final terms for restructuring the debt.

Eurotunnel told Reuters on Wednesday that talks with the banking consortium were making progress but had not been completed yet. "Our conversations with the banks are continuing and advancing very well but we cannot confirm at the moment that we have reached agreement," said a Eurotunnel spokeswoman in Paris.
Eurotunnel's London office indicated there would be an update on the debt situation in the annual results next week.
Banking sources had also said the steering committee of 20 instructing banks for Eurotunnel will meet to assess the debt deal terms ahead of the results on April 24.
But the key issue overshadowing the debt deal is the outcome of the joint Anglo-French governmental Channel Tunnel Safety Authority (CTSA) report into last November's tunnel fire.

Eurotunnel's own publication of an internal inquiry in recent weeks cleared the company's systems and equipment of any blame for causing the fire which caused major damage to one of the main tunnels, as wll as damaging rolling stock.
But the Kent Fire Brigade in southern England, which helped put out the fire, has said the design of Eurotunnel's open-sided freight carriages fanned the flames and created a "blow-torch" effect.
The brigade wants Eurotunnel to change the design of of its carriages -- a costly move which Eurotunnel is resisting.
But the key issue is whether the CTSA will back the fire brigade on this or Eurotunnel. Eurotunnel has said it is confident of being cleared by the CTSA.

A spokesman for the Kent Fire Brigade told Reuters on Friday that the final draft of the CTSA report has been drawn up and said it was not expected to be published before the British election on May 1.
Analysts will also be looking for reassurance on how quickly Eurotunnel can rebuild its freight business once it re-opens before the middle of June.
"We will want more financial information on how quickly freight traffic can be restored this year," said Richard Hannah of UBS.
